title: Redwood security review - SSO/SCIM & RBAC (HelixBank)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked HelixBank security and platform team through SSO (SAML) requirements, SCIM provisioning approach, and Redwood RBAC model. Key concerns: attribute mappings for groups, SCIM user sync frequency, least-privilege role definitions, audit log retention and encryption (KMS), and data residency. Next steps: share SAML metadata + ACS/Entity URLs, provide SCIM sample mappings and a demo tenant, and draft RBAC role templates for HelixBank to review. A short POC for SCIM push and a follow-up RBAC walkthrough were agreed.
next_steps: Maya: Send SAML metadata and ACS/Entity URLs + SSO integration guide by 2026-12-08
Aiden: Provide SCIM attribute mapping template and demo tenant credentials by 2026-12-10
Maya/Aiden: Share RBAC role templates and example least-privilege policies by 2026-12-13
Laura: Share HelixBank required user attributes, group naming conventions, and compliance questions by 2026-12-09
Schedule: 30-min follow-up demo for SCIM provisioning and RBAC review week of 2026-12-14
action_items: Maya Chen: Share SSO/SAML integration guide and SAML metadata by 2026-12-08
Aiden Park: Provide sample SCIM user and group mapping and push demo account by 2026-12-10
Laura Kim: Provide list of required RBAC roles and least-privilege policy doc by 2026-12-13
Rafael Ortiz: Coordinate dev test account and confirm IP allowlist for SCIM by 2026-12-11
transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Maya, I run the AE motion for Redwood. Today Aiden from our SE team and I will go through SSO and SCIM setup and then talk RBAC.
00:12 Laura (HelixBank): Hi thanks, Laura here, head of security. We've got Rafael, Nisha, and Samir on the call too.
00:20 Aiden (Redwood SE): Quick intro - I'll cover the SCIM endpoints, attribute mappings, and show how group sync works, and then we'll map that back to role-based access inside Redwood.
00:32 Maya: Super. Outline - SSO/SAML requirements, attribute list, SCIM provisioning options (push vs pull), group sync, RBAC roles and least-privilege patterns, audit logs & encryption, and data residency.
01:05 Samir (HelixBank): High level - HelixBank is SOC 2 Type II, prepping for ISO 27001; we need to ensure logs capture token-level events and that customer-managed KMS can be used for sensitive model keys.
01:22 Aiden: Understood. We'll cover KMS and audit log retention - Redwood supports customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we have a dedicated path with HSM-backed KMS - we'll share the KMS whitepaper.
01:37 Laura: Ok. On SSO - we use Okta - we want automated provisioning via SCIM and group-based role mapping.
01:45 Maya: Great, Okta is common. For SAML we need the IdP metadata from you, the ACS URL and Entity ID we'll provide. Typical attributes we recommend: email (NameID or attribute), firstName, lastName, and groups.
01:58 Nisha (HelixBank): For groups - we have nested groups and a few service accounts; can Redwood handle nested group membership?
02:08 Aiden: We flatten nested groups during SCIM sync by default but we can preserve path-like group names. The important piece is the attribute mapping - we can map Okta's group 'memberOf' to Redwood groups. There's sometimes transcription oddities with product names - apologies if I say 'Redwood Runtime' weirdly.
02:30 Rafael: How often does the SCIM sync run? We have frequent HR-driven changes and want near real-time provisioning.
02:40 Aiden: Push provisioning is best for near real-time - Okta push will call our SCIM endpoint on create/update/delete. Polling is possible but we recommend push. Rate limits: for hosted tenants we have conservative limits but for enterprise Dedicated customers we can increase them. We'll include throttling guidance.
03:02 Laura: Does SCIM support de-provisioning and group-to-role mapping?
03:10 Maya: Yes, de-provisioning for user lifecycle is supported. For role mapping we usually map Okta groups to Redwood roles - e.g., a group named 'rdw-admins' -> Redwood 'org_admin' role, 'rdw-ops' -> 'operator' role. We'll send sample JSON for mapping.
03:31 Samir: Regarding RBAC - we need least-privilege breakdown and justification to auditors. What roles are available out-of-the-box?
03:40 Aiden: Out-of-the-box we ship conservative roles: org_admin, model_deployer, operator, viewer, billing_admin (if you require). Customers can create custom roles with fine-grained permissions (deployment create, model change, logs access, billing view, keys management).
03:57 Laura: Can we restrict model deployment to a subset of models or specific namespaces? We have compliance models that have PII and others that are public.
04:09 Aiden: Yes - RBAC is resource-scoped. You can limit deployment capabilities to specific projects/namespaces and even create allowlists for model families. We'll attach a policy example showing model-scoped permissions.
04:26 Rafael: Audit logs - what level of granularity? We need token-level for forensic analysis (who called what model, timestamps, input hash ideally).
04:38 Maya: We capture request metadata: user id, role, endpoint, model id, request timestamp, and response metadata. We avoid storing raw PII in hosted logs unless configured. For higher fidelity we can configure payload hashing and store denormalized metadata in audit events. For Private we can push logs to customer SIEM via syslog/S3.
04:59 Samir: Are logs immutable and are they signed? Auditors ask about tamper evidence.
05:06 Aiden: We provide append-only log storage patterns and can integrate with your S3 bucket and object lock, or forward to your SIEM with TLS and signing. We can also provide export of logs for retention and audit.
05:24 Nisha: Encryption/KMS - we need to know if Redwood can use our KMS (AWS KMS or on-prem HSM) for model keys and for encrypting persisted artifacts.
05:34 Maya: For Private deployments yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; for Dedicated we support bring-your-KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) via integration; hosted has a managed KMS but we can offer CMK wraps in some enterprise agreements. We'll follow up with the KMS integration doc.
05:51 Laura: Data residency - HelixBank requires EU data to stay in EU region for EU customers. How granular is regional routing?
06:00 Aiden: We support region pinning at the tenant or route level. Requests can be routed to EU-only capacity. We'll provide the region mapping doc and SLA implications, e.g., latency trade-offs.
06:14 Rafael: Back to SAML - we need the exact attribute names Okta should send. We have a few service accounts that shouldn't map to interactive user roles.
06:24 Aiden: We'll recommend NameID=email for SAML; attributes: email, givenName, familyName, groups. For service accounts you can set an attribute or group prefix like 'svc_' and we can ignore or map those to a machine/service-role.
06:41 Laura: SCIM schema - can you show an example of a user object and group object?
06:45 Aiden: Yep - user: id, userName (email), externalId, active, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work,value=email], groups (list of group IDs). Group: id, displayName, members[]. We'll attach the full mapping.
07:05 Maya: FYI for auditing - we recommend enabling 'admin change' logging: role grant/revoke events, key rotations, and model rollback triggers.
07:17 Samir: On retention - recommended default retention for audit logs? We typically need 7 years for some finance use-cases.
07:24 Aiden: Redwood default retention for hosted logs is 90 days; enterprise customers can configure retention and export to your long-term S3 or SIEM. We often set up automated exports for 7-year compliance buckets.
07:37 Nisha: During SCIM provisioning, what about password sync or federated login - do you manage passwords?
07:43 Maya: No password management; auth is via SAML/SSO. SCIM only manages identities/profiles and group membership. Passwords remain in IdP.
07:52 Rafael: Can we demo SCIM push and show group->role mapping?
07:55 Aiden: Yes - we can spin up a demo tenant and show Okta push provisioning creating users and groups and mapping them to roles. That will be the follow-up action.
08:08 Laura: A question on least privilege - auditors want to avoid admin proliferation. Do you have role attestation or review tooling?
08:17 Aiden: We have role audit reports and can export current role assignments. We don't automatically require annual attestation but we can include the data in your attestation workflow; some customers use periodic exports and integrate with their IAM governance tooling.
08:34 Maya: Also note SSO session length controls - you can enforce session durations from the IdP or from Redwood for the console sessions; API tokens have separate TTLs and can be restricted to IP ranges.
08:48 Samir: About API keys and tokens - can RBAC restrict token scopes to read-only for monitoring teams?
08:54 Aiden: Yes tokens are scoped. We support service tokens with fine-grained scopes: generate-only-for-embeddings, generate-only-for-chat, read-logs-only, etc. We'll include examples.
09:10 Laura: Any customer-managed network constraints - do you support IP allowlists for SCIM callbacks?
09:16 Aiden: Yes, we support IP allowlisting and mutual TLS for SCIM endpoints for extra security. We'll need the HelixBank toolchain IP ranges to configure.
09:28 Nisha: For compliance, do you provide SOC 2 and pen test reports?
09:33 Maya: We can provide SOC 2 Type II reports under NDA and our pen test summary. We'll attach the links in the follow-up.
09:41 Rafael: Regarding SCIM user attribute sync: what about custom attributes like employee_id, department, manager?
09:48 Aiden: We support custom attributes; SCIM extension schema allows custom attributes, and we can map them into user metadata. Useful for role rules based on department.
10:02 Samir: On encryption in transit - are push notifications and SCIM performed over TLS 1.2/1.3?
10:08 Maya: Yes, TLS 1.2+ required and we prefer 1.3. Mutual TLS is available for dedicated enterprise.
10:18 Laura: Aiden, can you walk through an example mapping: Okta group 'hb_prod_admins' maps to Redwood org_admin, Okta group 'hb_deployers' maps to model_deployer scoped to project X?
10:29 Aiden: Sure - example: SCIM group displayName -> 'hb_prod_admins'; mapping rule: if group == 'hb_prod_admins' assign role 'org_admin'. For scoped mapping, include resource_id in mapping JSON, e.g., {"group":"hb_deployers","role":"model_deployer","scope":{"project":"payments-service"}}. We'll send the JSON example.
10:53 Laura: That helps. For nested groups we discussed flattening; what about name collisions?
11:00 Aiden: We recommend prefixing Redwood groups with 'rdw_' for clarity, or provide canonicalization rules. We'll include a recommended naming convention doc.
11:12 Nisha: On the SCIM rate limits again - for large orgs we might provision tens of thousands of users. Any batch endpoints?
11:20 Aiden: We support bulk user endpoints for initial sync and then delta push for changes. We'll provide best practices for initial ingest vs ongoing provisioning.
11:33 Samir: On the RBAC side, are there audit hooks for policy changes? We need to know when a role is modified.
11:39 Maya: Yes, role create/update/delete events are logged and can be shipped to your SIEM, and we can include who made the change (email + user id) and IP.
11:48 Rafael: Regarding KMS key rotation - does Redwood support automatic rotation and will that break active tokens?
11:55 Aiden: We support key rotation with a key versioning approach; active tokens are re-wrapped and we have a window for rotation to avoid disruption. We'll include a KMS rotation playbook.
12:09 Laura: For the POC, we want to test Okta->Redwood SCIM push for a small group and validate RBAC mapping, and then test de-provisioning. Does that sound ok?
12:18 Maya: Absolutely. Proposed plan: we'll provide SAML metadata and SCIM demo tenant, HelixBank config Okta and test users, then run the push and verify role assignments.
12:27 Nisha: Who will have access to the demo tenant? We need to ensure it's isolated and not on our prod data.
12:33 Aiden: Demo tenant is isolated. We'll provision a sandbox with synthetic data and limited retention.
12:41 Samir: One minor point - for compliance we may need signed agreements on log retention and access. Can you provide contract language or a SOC2 addendum?
12:49 Maya: Yes we have an enterprise addendum template for retention and logs. We'll loop legal if you want.
12:56 Laura: Ok, can you also confirm we can set conditional access based on IP or device posture?
13:02 Aiden: Conditional access is primarily enforced at the IdP layer; you can combine IdP signals with Redwood network controls like IP allowlists and session TTLs.
13:12 Maya: Quick note - when you configure SAML, some IdPs expect the ACS URL to only accept POST binding; we support POST and Redirect bindings but we'll confirm the exact endpoints.
13:23 Laura: Great. Any known gotchas?
13:27 Aiden: Two common ones: 1) mismatched NameID/attribute (email vs username) - ensure Okta NameID matches the SCIM userName; 2) group name variants - use consistent group naming for mapping.
13:40 Rafael: For audit evidence, will you provide proof of configuration change dates for SSO/SCIM setup?
13:47 Maya: Yes - configuration changes are logged with timestamps and user ids; we'll export a change log for the auditor.
13:55 Samir: Next steps recap?
14:00 Maya: We'll send SAML metadata, SCIM mapping JSON, RBAC role templates, KMS integration doc, SOC2 report link, and spin up demo tenant. Follow-up 30-min for SCIM demo week of 2026-12-14.
14:12 Laura: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
14:18 Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up.
14:20 [call ends]
